cards.title: Shadow/Radiant Moves
cards.text:
It allows the Pokémon to learn a Shadow Move. These moves, which can only be learned through this perk, are super effective against any Pokémon, regardless of its type.

For balancing purposes, all Shadow Moves have a maximum of 10 PP.

cards.title: Weathersync
cards.text:
This perk allows Pokémon to change one of their types to match the weather or terrain type that is currently active. If both weather and terrain are active at the same time, both types can be changed.

You can choose whether or not to activate this perk.

cards.title: Callforma
cards.text:
This perk allows you to summon a clone (a dummy version with no personality) of a character your character has befriended. This clone will possess the same abilities and moves as the original character.

The clone disappears if it takes damage or if the battle ends. Summoning it takes one turn and can only be done once per floor.

cards.title: Make Believe
cards.text:
This perk allows you to create a second version of your movepool; however, you can slightly alter the moves to give them different effects. Some examples would be Flamethrower becoming a Water-type move, or Blizzard, instead of having a chance to freeze, now having the ability to paralyze.

In battle, you can only switch between your movepool versions once. Once you've switched, it will remain that way for the rest of the battle. PP is shared between both movepool versions.

> If you choose this perk, you will have to submit the list of altered moves for approval.

cards.title: Mega-Evolution
cards.text:
You can Mega Evolve regardless of whether the parts of your fusion already possess a Mega Evolution or not. This Mega Evolution can result not only in a change to stats but also a change to your Pokémon's Common Battle Ability.

Mega Evolution lasts for the entire floor, but has a cooldown for the next floor.

> If you want to use this perk, you will need to submit the new common ability and the change in stats that your character will acquire upon mega-evolving.

cards.title: Z-Move
cards.text:
You can equip a Z-Move as if it were an extra move. You can use any Z-Move, regardless of whether your type allows it or not. However, it can only be used once per battle.

You start with one Z-Move of your choice, but you can obtain more later by completing missions. You can switch your Z-Move by switching the Z-Crystal you have equipped.

cards.title: Dynamax-Gigantamax
cards.text:
Like regular Gigantamax/Dynamax, you will take the form of a giant version of your Pokémon for 3 turns, changing your movepool to that of the Dynamax version.

However, your increased size means that all moves directed at you now have a 100% chance to hit, regardless of modifiers or abilities.

cards.title: Terastallization
cards.text:
It retains the effects of normal Terastallization, meaning your Pokémon will become mono-type but will keep the STAB of its original main type plus the STAB of the Teratype.

Once activated, it will last for the entire battle.

cards.title: Normal
cards.text: Can more easily adjust to certain environments, though at a lesser amount than other abilities dedicated to specific environments.

cards.title: Fire
cards.text: Slightly warmer than the average mon. Can tolerate fire, and swim in magma.

cards.title: Water
cards.text: Able to swim/breathe/dive underwater for far longer periods of time than other Pokémon.

cards.title: Electric
cards.text: Surrounded by a light layer of electric fuzz that helps detect incredibly close people. Concentrate this fuzz into electricity that can emit light and shock people, as a weak shock nowhere near the power of an actual move.

cards.title: Grass
cards.text: More in tune with plantlife, able to nurture and control its growth to fit desires.

cards.title: Ice
cards.text: Naturally cools down surroundings. Can tolerate freezing temperatures, and easily travel in snowy/icy zones.

cards.title: Fighting
cards.text: Can destroy large obstacles blocking paths. Your opponent cannot use foul, unusual tricks in duels you start, an example being having an ally of theirs attack you from the shadows.

cards.title: Poison
cards.text: Can absorb poison from allies to help them recover. With enough poison absorbed, can create a foul barrier that non-poison type amalgams refuse to cross.

cards.title: Ground
cards.text: Can dig and move around underground. However, some surfaces will be too hard to break through.

cards.title: Flying
cards.text: Can fly around, and tolerate difficult flying conditions like hailstorms, sandstorms, or similar.

cards.title: Psychic
cards.text: Can communicate telepathically with other Pokémon. Pokémon who lack telepathy can still respond by concentrating very hard on answering, but cannot start telepathic communication themselves.

cards.title: Bug
cards.text: Leave lingering messages behind for other bug types through pheromones.

cards.title: Rock
cards.text: More in tune with the earth and able to more easily find valuable gems while exploring.

cards.title: Ghost
cards.text: Gain the ability to levitate small/medium things, and can become intangible for a short time. If in a solid object when intangibility ends, teleport to the last location you were able to be in normally.

cards.title: Dragon
cards.text: Understand and peer through the veil of comprehension to more easily understand what is hidden to others.

cards.title: Dark
cards.text: More easily able to adjust and handle being in lightless areas with the ability to see in the darkness.

cards.title: Steel
cards.text: Alter and adjust the shape of non-living metal to your will. Stronger metals are more difficult to manipulate.

cards.title: Fairy
cards.text: You can conjure objects from your memory and make them appear out of thin air for a short time. Unfortunately, these objects have no special effects nor work as intended, even if their real-life counterparts did. They still retain their physical structure, though.
